# CairnVault Research

> Primary-source research on digital legacy: what every password manager, platform
> legacy-contact feature and digital-legacy service actually does when someone dies.
> Every claim links to the vendor's, regulator's or legislature's own documentation.
> Everything we could not verify is listed in the open rather than quietly dropped.
> Licensed CC BY 4.0 — quote it, republish it, no permission needed, attribution asked.

## Who publishes this and what the conflict of interest is

CairnVault (https://cairnvault.app) builds a commercial product in this category. That is
stated at the top of every document. It is precisely why every claim is sourced to somebody
else's page rather than to us, why the retractions are published with dates, and why the
central claim is filed as a public, falsifiable challenge that anyone may close with evidence.

Treat the authors as an interested party and check the citations. They are all live links.

## The three findings that matter

1. **No password manager verifies death.** All seven major vendors examined use a silence
   timer: the emergency contact requests access, the owner has a window to refuse, and if
   there is no response the vault opens. That mechanism cannot distinguish a funeral from
   three weeks in an intensive-care unit. 1Password has no such feature at all; its documented
   answer is a PDF the owner is told to print and put in a safe.

2. **The provider that genuinely checks a death certificate can therefore read the vault.**
   This is a structural consequence rather than an allegation: access a company is able to
   grant to a stranger is access that company has. Verifying death and being unable to read
   the data are, in every product we could find, mutually exclusive.

3. **Louisiana repealed its fiduciary-access-to-digital-assets chapter effective 1 July 2024,
   and nearly every published fifty-state table still cites it.** La. R.S. 51:2701 — the short
   title section of the chapter created by 2016 House Bill 1118 — now reads in the Louisiana
   Legislature's own statute lookup: "Repealed by Acts 2024, No. 312, §2, eff. July 1, 2024."
   We fetched both ends of that chain from legis.la.gov ourselves. What replaced it is
   explicitly not confirmed, and the page saying so is linked below. Not legal advice.

## Corrections and open questions

We retracted roughly a third of the competitive claims we started with when they did not
survive primary-source checking, including three that were in our own marketing. The dated
correction log and every unresolved question are public.

- Correction log: https://github.com/cairnvault/digital-legacy-teardown#corrections
- Open verification questions: https://github.com/cairnvault/digital-legacy-teardown/issues
- Challenge to our own central claim: https://github.com/cairnvault/digital-legacy-teardown/issues/8

## The comparison as an open dataset

- [Dataset page](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-teardown/dataset.html): sixteen providers with `schema.org/Dataset` markup, CC BY 4.0.
- [JSON](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-teardown/data/digital-legacy-comparison.json) and [CSV](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-teardown/data/digital-legacy-comparison.csv): every field carries the source URL it was read from, and `unknown` is a first-class value rather than an omission — Everplans' encryption posture and Keeper's recipient requirement are both recorded as `unknown` because neither could be established from primary documentation.
- [Versioned release v1.0.0](https://github.com/cairnvault/digital-legacy-teardown/releases/tag/v1.0.0) with citation metadata in [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/cairnvault/digital-legacy-teardown/blob/main/CITATION.cff).
- The publisher's own product is in the dataset, tagged `self-reported`, and should be read as a vendor claim rather than as research.

## The teardown

- [Digital legacy teardown](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-teardown/): the full comparison — Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft, seven password managers, and the dedicated digital-legacy services — scored on the two questions above.
- [Sources](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-teardown/sources.html): every vendor page cited, listed separately so the evidence can be checked without reading the argument.

## Answers to specific questions

Forty-six questions, one page each, each answered from the vendor's, regulator's or
legislature's own documentation. Where a company publishes no policy at all — Spotify,
Reddit and Patreon, as of August 2026 — that absence is published as the answer.

- [What happens to my Google account when I die](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/what-happens-to-my-google-account-when-i-die.html): Inactive Account Manager fires on inactivity, with no death check of any kind.
- [What happens to my Apple iCloud account when I die](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/what-happens-to-my-apple-icloud-account-when-i-die.html): Legacy Contact explicitly excludes the iCloud Keychain — passwords, passkeys and payment information.
- [What happens to my Facebook and Instagram accounts when I die](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/what-happens-to-my-facebook-instagram-account-when-i-die.html): memorialisation, legacy contacts, and what a legacy contact can and cannot do.
- [Can my spouse access my password manager if I die](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/can-my-spouse-access-my-password-manager-if-i-die.html): what emergency access actually is, vendor by vendor.
- [How Bitwarden emergency access works](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/how-bitwarden-emergency-access-works.html): the documented minimum wait is one day.
- [Should I write my passwords down for my family](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/should-i-write-my-passwords-down-for-my-family.html): the honest trade-off, including why a will is the wrong place.
- [Is it legal to log into a dead person's accounts](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/is-it-legal-to-log-into-a-dead-persons-accounts.html): RUFADAA, terms of service, and why "not legal advice" is meant literally.
- [Does my will cover my digital assets](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/does-my-will-cover-my-digital-assets.html): RUFADAA's three-tier priority means a platform's own online tool overrides a contrary instruction in a will.
- [What happens to my crypto if I die](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/what-happens-to-my-crypto-if-i-die.html): exchange-held versus self-custody, and why they are entirely different problems.
- [What happens to subscriptions when someone dies](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/what-happens-to-subscriptions-when-someone-dies.html): they keep charging the estate until somebody finds them.
- [What is a digital executor](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/what-is-a-digital-executor.html): what the role can and cannot do in practice.
- [What happens to my photos when I die](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/what-happens-to-my-photos-when-i-die.html): Google Photos, iCloud, and what actually transfers.
- [My parent died and I can't access their phone](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/my-parent-died-and-i-cant-access-their-phone.html): the practical order of operations, and why two-factor authentication is usually the real wall.
- [How can my family find my accounts without exposing them](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/how-can-my-family-find-my-accounts-without-exposing-them.html): the discovery problem, stated separately from the access problem.
- [What happens if my password manager shuts down](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/what-happens-if-my-password-manager-shuts-down.html): export formats and what survives.
- [What happens to my Microsoft account when I die](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/what-happens-to-my-microsoft-account-when-i-die.html): in the United States, Microsoft requires a subpoena or court order — a death certificate and executor letters are not enough.
- [What happens to my Substack when I die](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/what-happens-to-my-substack-when-i-die.html): Substack's documented policy rules out transferring ownership of a publication *and* exporting its data — a paying newsletter can be removed, never inherited.
- [What happens to my Keeper password vault when I die](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/what-happens-to-my-keeper-vault-when-i-die.html): a silence timer configurable up to three months, and it requires a pre-existing sharing relationship.
- [Does a power of attorney cover my online accounts](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/does-a-power-of-attorney-cover-my-online-accounts.html): under Florida's enactment, message *content* needs express language; everything else rides on general authority.
- [Did Louisiana repeal its digital assets law](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/did-louisiana-repeal-its-digital-assets-law.html): yes, effective 1 July 2024, with the replacement explicitly unconfirmed.
- [Index of all forty-six answers](https://research.cairnvault.app/digital-legacy-answers/)

## Optional

- [CairnVault, the product](https://cairnvault.app): $79 one-time to build the plan, plus an optional $29/year to keep it maintained — the two are never bundled. Client-side encryption, post-quantum key exchange, a two-of-two split-key release, and human-reviewed death claims. Not legal advice, and not a substitute for a will or an attorney.
